s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic respiratory symptoms with systemic lymphadenopathy and multi-organ involvement
salient_findings: Difficulties in breathing, cough, and expectoration for more than 30 days
Fever for more than 15 days
Multiple enlarged lymph nodes in the neck and abdomen regions
Cavities in the right upper anterior mediastinum and nodular shadow in the lower part of both lungs
Bilateral adrenal masses and bone destruction
key_facts: Presented with difficulties in breathing, cough, and expectoration
Past medical history of hyperuricemia for 5 years
Multiple enlarged lymph nodes in the neck and abdomen regions
Cavities in the right upper anterior mediastinum
Nodular shadow in the lower part of both lungs
Bone destruction of right clavicle and thoracic 11 right pedicle
Lymphadenopathy in neck and abdomen regions
Lesions in right lobe of thyroid gland

shortlist.label: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Multiple enlarged lymph nodes, lymphadenopathy, and lesions in various organs

shortlist.label: Hodgkin lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Cavities in the right upper anterior mediastinum and nodular shadow in the lower part of both lungs

shortlist.label: Tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic respiratory symptoms and fever for more than 15 days

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of multiple enlarged lymph nodes, cavities in the mediastinum, nodular shadows in the lungs, and bilateral adrenal masses, along with the biopsy findings of proliferative lymphoid tissues and singular large heterotypic proliferative lymphoid cells, are highly suggestive of Non-Hodgkin lymphoma.

rejected.label: Hodgkin lymphoma
rejected.why: While lymphadenopathy is common in Hodgkin lymphoma, the biopsy findings and the presence of cavities in the mediastinum are less typical for this condition.

rejected.label: Lymphomatoid granulomatosis
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with lung nodules and skin lesions, which are not the primary findings in this case.

rejected.label: Tuberculosis
rejected.why: The presence of fever and cough could suggest tuberculosis, but the biopsy findings and imaging studies do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: Sarcoidosis can cause lymphadenopathy and lung involvement, but the biopsy findings of proliferative lymphoid tissues and the presence of cavities in the mediastinum are not characteristic of this condition.
